beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense image carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process updates it repeatedly before decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method separates the dense image representation from the compact thought process that updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. The window step partitions those features for local processing. The DQ-CTM stage runs repeated ticks over the windows. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolved image. The recurrence returns to the DQ-CTM thought stage, with parameters shared across ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier through shared DQ-CTM ticks
params.note: The loop is only around the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as a dense encoder field, and window partitioning preserves every token for the thought process.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The equation defines the dense carrier before the compact thought process reads it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition operates on that field while keeping every token in the carrier.

params.headline: The window tokens come from a dense encoded field

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; its parameter count is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1, the second largest of the five listed methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not as evidence that the method is cheap. CATANet is the smallest model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is almost the same size at 0.550 million. IMDN is larger at 0.715 million. DQ-CTM-SR is second largest at 1.129 million. CARN is the largest model in this set at 1.592 million.
